text:
unconventional advice but if ur younger and u read a lot of books, surround urself w friends who read books...the gap widens out HARD as u progress from say age 20 to age 40.

sort of ties into the "choose ur gradient" theme

because you will see some guys that are 40 with the mind of a 50-60 year old, and then you have a lot of guys that are 40, but they still have the same brain as when they were 20.

they never changed, never updated any of their views or beliefs...zero grasp of nuance...it expresses itself in more ways than I can put words to.

books are what give u the courage to stand alone in a crowd. if u are steadily uploading 2000 years of history/biography/philosophy to ur subconscious, u will see time and time again that they are ur best guide for navigating life.

and so at some point, "hows bob doing," "oh he's the exact same" -- that becomes a real negative. u probably dont want to be the exact same at 40 as u were at 20.

ppl's attitude shapes their circumstance, everyone has similar career/family obligations but you'll see some ppl who always have an excuse for why they can't read books, whereas others always "play hurt," they always find a way to get shit done without complaining.

but all things compound, and honestly, I’m not sure anything compounds like reading books…knowledge and wisdom go exponential so goddamn fast that it’s hard to believe.

quotedTweet.text:
life isn’t "choose your own adventure," but it IS “choose your own gradient”

at all times you can adjust the difficulty level, the slope, the extent to which u live outside ur comfort zone, in each 24-hour block that we are allotted.

you can either push yourself on a daily basis, or you can never push at all.

make it as steep or as flat as you'd like...the truth is that its going to be hard either way.

many ppl run it at flat, when counterintuitively, flat may be the worst option.

first, because inertia and ennui become the challenge. they substitute for the degrees of the gradient, and they cause far more gloom and despair than any steep climb.

second, because once you reach the end of life, you look back across the flat stretch of land -- the gradient prairie -- and u realize that u never did any of the things you said you'd do.

"Some people die at 25," they say, "and we don't bury them until 75."

so while u cant control others, and u never want to go around telling ppl how to live their life

what u CAN control is who u surround yourself with. and far more important than a lot of the other shit people prioritize... is finding ppl who play the same game, on the same wavelength, and who approach each 24-hour block on the same gradient that you do.
